title: Prioritization: Surfacing & Routing Cutlist — Sprint 23 (Jul 2026)
body:
Context:
We have a growing number of customer requests and internal wishes for better surfacing of routing policies, model fallbacks, and per-route cost visibility in the Console. This doc captures the cutlist for Sprint 23 (2-week) and the triage rationale for each candidate ticket/idea. Goal: pick a minimal set of deliverables that unblock the Dedicated & Private sales motion while keeping a usable UX for self-serve hosted users.

Sprint objectives (high-level):
- Make routing policy status visible on route details page (quick health + active fallback info).
- Add compact cost-per-token indicator for route list and route details (alpha).
- Clean up the rollout/canary UX so engineers can create a weighted canary without leaving the route editor.
- Defer deep audit log retention UI and full-blown route analytics to next sprint.

Decision principles used for triage:
- Customer impact: does this unblock a paying sale or large customer pilot?
- Time-to-value: can design+dev deliver within the sprint with 1 engineer + 0.5 designer?
- Risk: does the change require infra changes or migrations?
- Consistency: fits into current Console patterns (list/details/editor).

Cutlist (accepted items):
1) RDW-4217: Route details — display active routing policy and fallback chain (alpha)
   - Owner: Marco Reyes
   - Why: Sales asked for the ability to show customers what fallback model was used when origin capacity was low.
   - Scope: show a small badge area in the route header: current policy name, primary model, fallback list (collapsed), last-fallback-timestamp.
   - Wireframe notes: three-line header: route name + status badge; second line: model chip(s) with small chevron to expand fallback list.
   - Acceptance criteria: expanded fallback list shows up to 5 variants with short reasons; clicking a variant opens model details side-sheet.
   - Dependencies: model catalog API endpoint (stable), small backend flag to surface last_fallback_ts; no infra deployment.
   - Triage: accept (low infra risk, high customer unblock).

2) RDW-4278: Route list — compact cost-per-token indicator and tooltip
   - Owner: Lena Cho
   - Why: product wants quick cost signal in list view to help customers find expensive routes.
   - Scope: add a right-aligned cost chip per row showing 1m-avg cost estimate (alpha), with tooltip explaining approximation and link to cost breakdown page.
   - Wireframe notes: cost chip uses same color semantics as SLO chips; tooltip contains sample calculation: tokens * model_price * batching_factor_est.
   - Acceptance criteria: chip shows with value or ‘—’ for routes without usage; tooltip links to cost breakdown anchor.
   - Dependencies: aggregated cost API; fallback to client-side calc if server not available.
   - Triage: accept (visible impact, low complexity).

3) RDW-4302: Route editor — inline weighted canary control + preview
   - Owner: Samir Patel
   - Why: engineers currently have to leave editor to create a canary. Single-screen flow reduces errors and supports quick rollouts.
   - Scope: add a new section in the route editor: 'Rollouts' with toggles for canary, numeric weight slider (0-100), and simple preview showing percentage of traffic per model.
   - Wireframe notes: slider with numeric input, confirm button labeled 'Create canary', inline validation showing conflicts with autoscale policies.
   - Acceptance criteria: create canary action triggers RDW API call and returns canary id; UI shows warning if weight > 50%.
   - Dependencies: route-rollout API (exists but needs a small change to accept inline payload).
   - Triage: accept (medium complexity, high UX improvement).

Cutlist (parked / deferred):
- RDW-4130: Full route analytics dashboard (defer to sprint 24). Rationale: large scope and requires infra indexing work.
- RDW-4172: Audit log retention UI for Private (defer). Rationale: enterprise-only and requires compliance vetting.
- RDW-4250: Model cost forecasting tool (defer to product Optimize roadmap).

Cutlist (blocked):
- RDW-4225: Prefetch KV cache visualization. Blocked by runtime telemetry API.

UX/wireframe quick sketches (detailed notes for designer):
- Route list row (compact): [Route name] [env tag] [SLO badge] ................ [cost chip]
  - cost chip hover: small modal with sample 24h cost, link to detailed view.
- Route details header: [Route name]  [STATUS: green/yellow/red]  [policy chip]  [last fallback: 2026-06-29 13:02 UTC]
  - Expand fallback: dropdown with 3–5 chips, each chip shows model + short reason (ex: capacity-fallback).
- Rollouts section inside route editor: vertical card with a slider, numeric field, and 'Preview' box showing small pie chart (labels: primary X%, fallback Y%). If user tries to set weight > 50% show inline helper text: 'Support is limited for >50% canary — check autoscale settings.'

Engineering notes and estimates (rough):
- RDW-4217: 1 FE dev (4 days) + 0.5 BE (1 day) + 1 designer (2 days) -> total ~7 dev-days
- RDW-4278: 1 FE dev (2 days) + 0.5 designer (1 day) -> total ~3 dev-days
- RDW-4302: 1 FE dev (5 days) + 0.5 BE (2 days) + 1 designer (3 days) -> total ~10 dev-days

Sprint capacity check:
- Team: 2 frontend engineers (available 6 dev-days each), 1 backend (8 dev-days), 1 designer (6 design-days).
- Sum planned dev-days: ~20; capacity available: FE 12 + BE 8 + Designer 6 = 26 -> Acceptable buffer.

Rollout / QA notes:
- Feature flags for all three items: console.routing_ui_v1, console.cost_chip_alpha, console.inline_rollout_editor.
- QA: add smoke tests to route list + details flows; basic e2e for canary creation and state display.
- Monitoring: add Sentry breadcrumbs for rollout create failure; track metric console.route_ui.errors.

Open questions / decisions to resolve this week:
- UX copy for cost tooltip: product to approve wording (Lena) by Tue 2026-07-06.
- Exact backend payload shape for inline rollout: engineering to propose contract by Wed 2026-07-07 (Samir).
- Should the cost chip show 24h or 7d avg? Decision: show 7d avg for stability; confirm by Thu 2026-07-08.

Next steps (this doc as checklist):
- [ ] Designer creates final mocks for RDW-4217, RDW-4278, RDW-4302 (due 2026-07-05).
- [ ] Backend PR to expose last_fallback_ts (RDW-4217) (due 2026-07-06).
- [ ] FE spike for cost calc fallback (client-side) (due 2026-07-05).
- [ ] Kickoff sync: product + eng + design on 2026-07-03 10:00 PT.

Notes to reviewers:
- This cutlist aims to be conservative: pick visible wins that help sales demos and reduce friction for platform engineers. If capacity shifts, we should drop RDW-4278 (cost chip) before dropping the route-fallback visibility or the inline rollout editor.

Quick links (for PRs, design, and tickets):
- Confluence: console-routing-design-v2
- JIRA: RDW-4217 (route fallback), RDW-4278 (cost chip), RDW-4302 (inline rollout)
- Slack thread: #prod-console-routing (see pinned messages)

Author note: drafted during grooming session on 2026-07-02; updated after dev estimates and design sync on 2026-07-08.
